text: Universal G length — exactly 2^ω+ω−1, attained by 2^(2^(ω−1)) words [foundationsChecks, exhaustive ω ≤ 4] — H1 confirmed as a theorem; de Bruijn is not just good but the only minimal-length universal family

Break-even region — exact for per-read ⌈·⌉ pointers; N = 2^(ω−1)+1 loses despite log2 N < ω [T3, table] — the ceiling halves the usable range; joint pointer coding recovers N < 2^ω but with vanishing gain

Encodable fraction vs saving — regime B meets it with equality: reachable fraction 2^−(m−1)(ω−k) = 2^−(mω−n) [T11] — the strided scheme is a perfect (waste-free) code onto its image; regime A with pointers wastes log2(N/p) bits/read
Pair coincidence — Pr[r_i = r_j] = 2^−ω exactly for all i ≠ j [T8] — second-order statistics are those of iid words; overlap acts only at third order
iid approximation of E[p] — |error| ≤ 0.370 words, relative ≤ 8·10^−5 at ω=14 [CHECKED ω ≤ 14] — use 2^ω(1−(1−2^−ω)^N); exact GO sum only needed for N ≲ 1
P[p = N] — exceeds it (0.8545 vs 0.7336, ω=8, n=20) [exhaustive] — window coincidences are positively correlated, so distinct-window events are more likely than iid predicts

Champernowne is the slowest natural example, not a typical one. T_ω = (ω−1)2^ω+ω+2 exactly (ω ≤ 12), 1.44× the coupon-collector time of a random sequence. The reason is mechanical: 0^ω is born in the number 2^ω, so it is always last.
note: Formula quoted and brute-forced; relayed, no direction opened (02 row 2)

text: The count of ω-complete G at length n_min+1 is 2^(2^(ω−1))·(11/2 − 2^(2−ω)), i.e. 11/2 times the de Bruijn count in the limit (L5); verified through ω = 7, not proved.

A de Bruijn word and an m-sequence are indistinguishable for every φ and bit-cost measurement although c differs (10 vs 9).

Where random G becomes ω-complete — n50/(2^ω ω ln2) = 1.44, 1.20, 1.09, 1.06, 1.05 at ω = 2, 4, 8, 10, 12 [atlas_threshold.csv, exact DP, first moment, MC] — the heuristic is right to leading order; the +0.37 (Gumbel median) shift matters until ω ≳ 10

Sharpness — transition width O(1) in N/2^ω, i.e. relative width 3.08/(ω ln2 + 0.37): 1.1 at ω=4, 0.44 at ω=10 [figure 3c] — the transition sharpens only like 1/ω: at ω = 10, n10 to n90 still spans 3 300 bits

Upper tail of the transition — exact ω = 3, 4 curves lie below Gumbel for x > 1 [figure 3b]; P[incomplete] decays at the ω-bonacci rate λ_ω/2 = 0.92, 0.96 — the last word to appear is almost always 0^ω or 1^ω (L9); exact n90 → n99 is 40 → 66 (ω=3) and 91 → 148 (ω=4) vs 19 and 38 predicted by Gumbel

Doubling-map lens, normal vs random — Champernowne T_ω = (ω−1)2^ω + ω + 2 exactly, 1/ln2 ≈ 1.44× slower than random, ≈ (ω−1)× slower than de Bruijn; √2 and π track random within one sd [figure 6] — normality is asymptotic equidistribution, not speed; a disjunctive sequence can need ≈ ω 2^ω bits, the structured ordering of Champernowne puts 0^ω last

m-sequence vs de Bruijn — identical κ profile except ω = 10 (1023 vs 1024 of 1024), identical E[L] (10.997 vs 10.998), identical φ distribution and bit cost for all W ≤ 16 [tables] — for every composition-style use the free LFSR sequence is as good as the optimal de Bruijn word; c(G) alone overstates the gap

Profile shape — unimodal for all 2^20 G; slope after the peak is 0 or −1 and exactly −1 beyond the longest repeated factor [figure 5, L3] — the (ω, p) plot of any finite G is a rise, an optional plateau, then n−ω+1; there are no other shapes

Compression of uniform targets by composition — mean bits ≥ 1.4 W for every family and every W = 8…16 (minimum 1.40 at W = 10, de Bruijn; 1.8 W at W = 16) [figure 8, table above] — consistent with foundations T4/T5 (no free lunch on uniform targets); composition is about expressibility, never about rate

Low complexity — T(p) = Σ Prim(q) f(a) f(b) reproduces all ten values 2 … 16 270 and equals the explicitly constructed set for 5 cells [lowcomplexity.py --quick] — the plateau is the set of "periodic core with a few arbitrary letters at each end" words; see L15

Weight, not Fine–Wilf, closes the proof of T1. The delicate configuration (the first window of G recurring in the right flank) is excluded by a parity fact: two distinct rotations of a primitive binary word cannot agree on q−1 positions, because they have equal Hamming weight, so their distance is even (Lemma II.6, case L).

All deeper overlap levels cancel in T2. Σ over edges of d_eᵀP^k d_e vanishes for every k ≥ 2 because the de Bruijn graph has exactly 2^k words of period k (and 2^(k+1) of period k+1) for the four overlap indicators; only k = 0 and k = 1 contribute.
note: T2 is carried (outline 2.2); the cancellation surprise is not

Low-complexity count — a complete proof; both unproved steps (flank windows distinct; no coincidence between a left and a right window) are Lemmas II.5 and II.6; machine-checked on 25 200 words [lowcomplexity_check.py] — T(p) is the number of "periodic core with a flanks on the left and b on the right"; no Fine–Wilf lemma is needed, only positions of period defects and one weight (parity) argument

Range of T1 — the proof uses p ≤ ω (j ≤ ω, s+q ≤ ω, bound (★)) and p ≤ n−ω (a repeat exists); outside, 0 violations of "count ≠ T(p)" except 9 sporadic cells [range_report, n ≤ 18] — the range is the natural domain of the proof; the sporadic cells (2ω+1, ω, ω+1) remain unexplained

Count at n = 2^ω+ω — exact for ω = 8; proof reduces to Q = Σ_e d_eᵀL⁺d_e = 3·2^(ω−2)−1, where only the overlap levels k = 0, 1 survive [complete_count.py] — the 11/2 = 2·2 + 3/2 arises from 2^(ω+1)·(1+…) at level 0 and a single level-1 correction; all deeper overlap sums cancel exactly

Entropy vs completeness — κ_G(ω) = 2^(−ω(1−D_G(ω))); h < 1 for every non-disjunctive G (proved, bound 1 + log2(1−2^−(c+1))/(c+1)); the sharper log2 λ_{c+1} is checked, not proved — the blue fraction of a barcode row decays like 2^(−(1−h)ω); c(G) finite already forces a Cantor set of dimension < 1

Topological vs measure entropy — a Bernoulli(θ) random sequence, 0 < θ < 1, contains every word, so p = 2^ω and h_G = 1 = dim X_G for every θ — the law is about the support of the orbit, not about typical blocks; typical-set rates are a measure-entropy matter (foundations Q4)

Finite-n resolution — true for h = 1 and golden mean (p_G = F_{ω+2} to ω = 22 at n = 2^21); false for h = 0 sequences, which are resolved up to ω ≈ n/R (Thue–Morse n = 128: to ω = 33) — the ceiling log2(n−ω+1)/ω binds only when p_∞(ω) ≳ n

Support completion for h < 1 — golden mean: T_ω ≈ 0.7–0.83 · ω F_{ω+2} (ω = 6…18) — the atlas threshold law holds with 2^ω replaced by the number of allowed words, up to a constant from the unequal word probabilities of the Parry measure
The only literal-scheme win on real data is a palette effect at ω = 24 on RGB bytes, not anything about windows of G.

Greedy SCS beat the polynomial path cover almost everywhere (up to 6.1× shorter) because concatenating trails wastes ω−1 junk bits per join; the "path cover ≤ greedy ≤ SCS" ordering in the roadmap is not a theorem for the heuristics (3 reversals).
The saving on the dictionary (up to ω-fold) is real in |G| terms but is cancelled by pointer growth in the one regime where it is large (Markov, ω = 24).

At ω = 32 greedy wins 0.667 vs 0.859 [CSV] — The dictionary saving is repaid by the larger pointer space whenever m/K is large; it wins only when K is close to m

Greedy at a byte-aligned width — MiniLM ω = 32 (one float32 per block): greedy |G| = 12.4M vs 6.1M at ω = 31, while 520,000 random 32-bit words give 6.7M (spot check, not in CSV) — Aligned prefixes (sign+exponent) are concentrated, so few suffix/prefix coincidences exist; real structure can make G longer than for random words

The existing term is better for four of seven objects. The atlas and framing already chose "complete", "coverage" and "composition"; a coinage would only add weight. The one real gap is a role-neutral noun for G.
note: imbrex adopted; the argument that existing terms are better is not carried

text: "Order" is already the de Bruijn word for the integer c(G) generalizes, so c(G) needs no coinage at all.

Compositional completeness is not a separate property (atlas L12: a-complete iff c(G) ≥ max a_i). Giving it its own head word would suggest otherwise; sharing the adjective "complete" is the honest naming.
The pointer map of regime A (rank and unrank) is Pingala's uddiṣṭa and naṣṭa, 2 300 years before this repository.

"cardinal sequence" as a name for G — Juhász and Weiss define cardinal sequences of compact scattered spaces; a 2024 arXiv paper continues the line — Collision with an established topology term. Reject

"generative sequence" / "generator sequence" — Convolutional codes build outputs by convolving the input with "generator sequences" g1, g2 over GF(2) — Regimes B and C are trellis codes, so a "generator sequence" is a different, standard object. "Generative" adds the LLM reading
"universal" for completeness — "k-subsequence universal" words (every word up to length k as a subsequence) have an active literature — Avoid "universal" for the factor property

"disjunctive" and "normal" — Disjunctive: infinite sequence containing every finite word (Jürgensen and Thierrin); weaker than Borel normality — Use for the c = ∞ limit only; they do not name finite G

"window" vocabulary — "Window complexity" is an existing complexity notion on infinite words (Cassaigne, Kaboré, Tapsoba) — Do not name any of the seven objects "window complexity" or "window profile"

"window property" — Golomb sequences: sliding a width-m window sees each nonzero m-tuple exactly once — Existing name for the exactly-once case (m-sequence, de Bruijn). Keep "complete" for the at-least-once case

Sanskrit exemplar — Earliest known de Bruijn-type sequence: the mnemonic yamātārājabhānasalagām, all eight length-3 patterns of short and long syllables; Pingala's prastāra lists all 2^n patterns — Structure-bearing exemplar for a footnote: the oldest scroll is a length-10 word with c = 3 at minimal length 2^3+3−1
"scroll" elsewhere — Rational normal scroll: a ruled surface in algebraic geometry — Mild, disjoint-field collision. Accept and note
"scroll coding" as a phrase — Web search returned only LZ77 and sliding-window patents, no use of the phrase — No collision found; evidence weak (see Provenance)
